2	
3	## Image-analysis method
4	
5	Van der Walt et al., “scikit-image: image processing in Python,” *PeerJ* 2,
6	e453 (2014). DOI: [10.7717/peerj.453](https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.453).
7	
8	The paper describes scikit-image as a collection of algorithms for scientific
9	image processing. The supplied source is the `measure` part of the project,
10	which turns a binary or intensity image into geometric and moment-based region
11	measurements.
12	
13	## The supplied microscopy data
14	
15	Muller et al., “Accurate evaluation of size and refractive index for spherical
16	objects in quantitative phase imaging,” *Optics Express* 26(8), 10729--10743
17	(2018). DOI: [10.1364/OE.26.010729](https://doi.org/10.1364/OE.26.010729).
18	
19	The image in `fixtures/cell.png` is the CC0 quantitative-phase cell image
20	distributed by scikit-image. Its documented native pixel spacing is 0.107
21	micrometers. The image is useful here because a microscope image is not merely
22	an array of abstract numbers: the distance represented by one row step and
23	one column step is part of the scientific data.
24	
25	## Coordinate and moment definitions
26	
27	For an image with dimension `D`, let a foreground sample at integer index
28	`i = (i_0, ..., i_{D-1})` have physical coordinate
29	
30	$$
31	x_k = i_k s_k,
32	$$
33	
34	where `s_k` is the sampling interval along axis `k`. If the image has a
35	non-unit intensity value `I(i)`, a raw image moment has the form
36	
37	$$
38	M_p = \sum_i I(i)\prod_k x_k^{p_k},
39	$$
40	
41	where `p` is a multi-index and `|p| = sum(p_k)`. The zeroth moment is the
42	total weight used by the image-moment convention. The centroid is the weighted
43	coordinate obtained from the first-order moments:
44	
45	$$
46	c_k = M_{e_k}/M_0.
47	$$
48	
49	Central moments use the same physical coordinates relative to that centroid:
50	
51	$$
52	\mu_p = \sum_i I(i)\prod_k (x_k-c_k)^{p_k}.
53	$$
54	
55	For a dimensionless normalized descriptor, a common change of measurement unit
56	must not change the answer. A useful convention is therefore to divide the
57	order-`|p|` spatial factor by a common unit scale `u` before applying the
58	mass/area normalization:
59	
60	$$
61	\nu_p = \frac{\mu_p/u^{|p|}}
62	              {M_0^{\,|p|/D+1}}.
63	$$
64	
65	The common scale removes a uniform change of units; the axis-specific values
66	still describe the physical shape of an anisotropically sampled object. In an
67	implementation with no separately supplied physical unit, a
68	deterministic common scale derived from the sampling intervals is needed; the
69	smallest interval is one valid convention because it leaves every interval
70	ratio explicit. The exact array layout and exponent ordering follow the source
71	docstrings and the standard image-moment convention.
72	
73	## Region geometry
74	
75	An inertia tensor is built from second central moments. Its eigenvalues encode
76	the spread of the object along its principal axes, so axis lengths, orientation,
77	and eccentricity must use the same physical coordinate system as the moments.
78	The physical area or volume of a foreground region is its sample count times
79	the product of the axis intervals. Changing the calibration changes metric
80	quantities such as distances and moments, but it does not change which integer
81	lattice sites belong to the segmented object. A conversion from sample
82	identity to physical location therefore has to keep its units explicit.
83	
84	Some raster-boundary quantities are defined by a discrete neighborhood and do
85	not have a generally valid anisotropic interpretation without an explicit
86	geometric model. A scientifically honest implementation may keep such a
87	restriction explicit rather than returning a silently misleading value.
88	
89	## Local documentation supplied with the source
90	
91	The relevant API contracts are in the docstrings of the supplied source,
92	especially the image-moment and region-measurement routines. For background,
93	the project documentation and the current API reference are available at:
94	
95	- https://scikit-image.org/docs/stable/api/skimage.measure.html
96	- https://scikit-image.org/docs/stable/auto_examples/segmentation/plot_regionprops.html

53	     * Centroid as: {``M[1, 0] / M[0, 0]``, ``M[0, 1] / M[0, 0]``}.

60	    coords : (N, D) double or uint8 array
61	        Array of N points that describe an image of D dimensionality in
62	        Cartesian space. A tuple of coordinates as returned by
63	        ``np.nonzero`` is also accepted as input.

66	        is not provided.

92	    rows 1 and 3) are zero when centered on the centroid, or center of mass,
93	    of the object (the default). If we break the symmetry by adding a new
94	    point, this no longer holds:

450	    """Compute the eigenvalues of the inertia tensor of the image.
451	
452	    The inertia tensor measures covariance of the image intensity along
453	    the image axes. (See `inertia_tensor`.) The relative magnitude of the
454	    eigenvalues of the tensor is thus a measure of the elongation of a
455	    (bright) object in the image.

457	    Parameters
458	    ----------
459	    image : array
460	        The input image.
461	    mu : array, optional
462	        The pre-computed central moments of ``image``.
463	    T : array, shape ``(image.ndim, image.ndim)``
464	        The pre-computed inertia tensor. If ``T`` is given, ``mu`` and
465	        ``image`` are ignored.
466	    spacing: tuple of float, shape (ndim, )
467	        The pixel spacing along each axis of the image.
468	
469	    Returns
470	    -------
471	    eigvals : list of float, length ``image.ndim``
472	        The eigenvalues of the inertia tensor of ``image``, in descending
473	        order.
474	
475	    Notes
476	    -----
477	    Computing the eigenvalues requires the inertia tensor of the input image.
478	    This is much faster if the central moments (``mu``) are provided, or,
479	    alternatively, one can provide the inertia tensor (``T``) directly.
480	    """
481	    if T is None:
482	        T = inertia_tensor(image, mu, spacing=spacing)
483	    eigvals = np.linalg.eigvalsh(T)
484	    # Floating point precision problems could make a positive
485	    # semidefinite matrix have an eigenvalue that is very slightly
486	    # negative. This can cause problems down the line, so set values
487	    # very near zero to zero.

233	def _inertia_eigvals_to_axes_lengths_3D(inertia_tensor_eigvals):
234	    """Compute ellipsoid axis lengths from inertia tensor eigenvalues.
235	
236	    Paramters
237	    ---------
238	    inertia_tensor_eigvals : seqeunce of float
239	        A sequence of 3 floating point eigenvalues, sorted in descending order.
240	
241	    Returns
242	    -------
243	    axis_lengths : list of float
244	        The ellipsoid axis lengths sorted in descending order.

246	    Notes
247	    -----
248	    Let a >= b >= c be the ellipsoid semi-axes and s1 >= s2 >= s3 be the
249	    inertia tensor eigenvalues.
250	
251	    The inertia tensor eigenvalues are given for a solid ellipsoid in [1]_.
252	    s1 = 1 / 5 * (a**2 + b**2)
253	    s2 = 1 / 5 * (a**2 + c**2)
254	    s3 = 1 / 5 * (b**2 + c**2)
255	
256	    Rearranging to solve for a, b, c in terms of s1, s2, s3 gives
257	    a = math.sqrt(5 / 2 * ( s1 + s2 - s3))
258	    b = math.sqrt(5 / 2 * ( s1 - s2 + s3))
259	    c = math.sqrt(5 / 2 * (-s1 + s2 + s3))
260

262	    lengths rather than the semi-axes lengths.

264	    References
265	    ----------
266	    ..[1] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_moments_of_inertia#List_of_3D_inertia_tensors  # noqa
267	    """
268	    axis_lengths = []
269	    for ax in range(2, -1, -1):
270	        w = sum(v * -1 if i == ax else v
271	                for i, v in enumerate(inertia_tensor_eigvals))
272	        axis_lengths.append(sqrt(10 * w))

738	        ``image`` and ``coords``.
739

741	    -------
742	    out_dict : dict

744	        property, one value per region. This dictionary can be used as input to
745	        pandas ``DataFrame`` to map property names to columns in the frame and
746	        regions to rows.

748	    Notes

750	    Each column contains either a scalar property, an object property, or an
751	    element in a multidimensional array.

754	    appear as a float or int array with that property name as key.

760	    {property_name}{separator}{elem_num0}{separator}{elem_num1} (for 2D

776	    >>> props  # doctest: +ELLIPSIS +SKIP

778	     'inertia_tensor-0-0': array([  4.012...e+03,   8.51..., ...]), ...

783	    obtain a clean DataFrame:

789	    0      1         4012.909888  ...                267.065503
790	    1      2            8.514739  ...                  2.834806
791	    2      3            0.666667  ...                  0.000000
792	    3      4            0.000000  ...                  0.000000
793	    4      5            0.222222  ...                  0.111111
794

797	    out = {}
798	    n = len(regions)
799	    for prop in properties:
800	        r = regions[0]
801	        # Copy the original property name so the output will have the

804	        # determine the current property name for any deprecated property.

828	            else:
829	                shape = (len(rp),)
830	
831	            # precompute property column names and locations
832	            modified_props = []
833	            locs = []
834	            for ind in np.ndindex(shape):

847	
848	            # add the columns to the output dictionary
849	            for i, modified_prop in enumerate(modified_props):

849	            for i, modified_prop in enumerate(modified_props):
850	                out[modified_prop] = column_data[:, i]

"""Independent reference implementation of calibrated region measurements.

Computes region properties from first principles using physical coordinates
x_k = i_k * s_k, per the paper's definitions.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import itertools
import numpy as np


def raw_moments(image, spacing, order=3, origin=None):
    """M_p = sum_i I(i) prod_k (i_k*s_k - origin_k)^{p_k} over local grid."""
    image = np.asarray(image, dtype=np.float64)
    ndim = image.ndim
    if origin is None:
        origin = np.zeros(ndim)
    grids = np.meshgrid(*[np.arange(n) * s - o
                          for n, s, o in zip(image.shape, spacing, origin)],
                        indexing='ij')
    M = np.zeros((order + 1,) * ndim)
    for powers in itertools.product(range(order + 1), repeat=ndim):
        term = image.copy()
        for ax, p in enumerate(powers):
            term = term * grids[ax] ** p
        M[powers] = term.sum()
    return M


def centroid_local(image, spacing, order=3):
    M = raw_moments(image, spacing, order=1)
    M0 = M[(0,) * image.ndim]
    out = []
    for ax in range(image.ndim):
        idx = [0] * image.ndim
        idx[ax] = 1
        out.append(M[tuple(idx)] / M0)
    return np.array(out)


def central_moments(image, spacing, order=3):
    c = centroid_local(image, spacing)
    return raw_moments(image, spacing, order=order, origin=c)


def normalized_moments(mu, spacing, order=3):
    ndim = mu.ndim
    nu = np.zeros_like(mu)
    mu0 = mu.ravel()[0]
    u = min(spacing)
    for powers in itertools.product(range(order + 1), repeat=ndim):
        p = sum(powers)
        if p < 2:
            nu[powers] = np.nan
        else:
            nu[powers] = (mu[powers] / u ** p) / mu0 ** (p / ndim + 1)
    return nu


def inertia_tensor(image, spacing, mu=None):
    ndim = image.ndim
    if mu is None:
        mu = central_moments(image, spacing, order=2)
    mu0 = mu[(0,) * ndim]
    T = np.zeros((ndim, ndim))
    second = []
    for ax in range(ndim):
        idx = [0] * ndim
        idx[ax] = 2
        second.append(mu[tuple(idx)])
    total = sum(second)
    for ax in range(ndim):
        T[ax, ax] = (total - second[ax]) / mu0
    for a, b in itertools.combinations(range(ndim), 2):
        idx = [0] * ndim
        idx[a] = 1
        idx[b] = 1
        T[a, b] = T[b, a] = -mu[tuple(idx)] / mu0
    return T

def moments_normalized(mu, order=3, spacing=None):
    """Calculate all normalized central image moments up to a certain order.

    Note that normalized central moments are translation and scale invariant
    but not rotation invariant.

    Parameters
    ----------
    mu : (M,[ ...,] M) array
        Central image moments, where M must be greater than or equal
        to ``order``.
    order : int, optional
        Maximum order of moments. Default is 3.
    spacing: tuple of float, shape (ndim, )
        The pixel spacing along each axis of the image. The central moments
        ``mu`` are assumed to have been computed with these same sampling
        intervals. Because a normalized moment must be dimensionless, the
        order ``|p|`` spatial factor is divided by the common length scale
        ``min(spacing)`` before the zeroth-moment normalization is applied.
        This leaves a uniform change of units without effect, while the
        ratios between the individual intervals remain visible in the result.

    Returns
    -------
    nu : (``order + 1``,[ ...,] ``order + 1``) array
        Normalized central image moments.

    References
    ----------
    .. [1] Wilhelm Burger, Mark Burge. Principles of Digital Image Processing:
           Core Algorithms. Springer-Verlag, London, 2009.
    .. [2] B. Jähne. Digital Image Processing. Springer-Verlag,
           Berlin-Heidelberg, 6. edition, 2005.
    .. [3] T. H. Reiss. Recognizing Planar Objects Using Invariant Image
           Features, from Lecture notes in computer science, p. 676. Springer,
           Berlin, 1993.
    .. [4] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Image_moment

    Examples
    --------
    >>> image = np.zeros((20, 20), dtype=np.double)
    >>> image[13:17, 13:17] = 1
    >>> m = moments(image)
    >>> centroid = (m[0, 1] / m[0, 0], m[1, 0] / m[0, 0])
    >>> mu = moments_central(image, centroid)
    >>> moments_normalized(mu)
    array([[       nan,        nan, 0.078125  , 0.        ],
           [       nan, 0.        , 0.        , 0.        ],
           [0.078125  , 0.        , 0.00610352, 0.        ],
           [0.        , 0.        , 0.        , 0.        ]])
    """
    if np.any(np.array(mu.shape) <= order):
        raise ValueError("Shape of image moments must be >= `order`")
    if spacing is None:
        spacing = np.ones(mu.ndim)
    nu = np.zeros_like(mu)
    mu0 = mu.ravel()[0]
    scale = min(spacing)
    for powers in itertools.product(range(order + 1), repeat=mu.ndim):
        if sum(powers) < 2:
            nu[powers] = np.nan
        else:
            nu[powers] = (mu[powers] / scale ** sum(powers)) / (
                mu0 ** (sum(powers) / nu.ndim + 1)
            )
    return nu

                             moments_central, moments_normalized, centroid,

FAILS = []
CHECKS = [0]


def check(cond, name, detail=""):
    CHECKS[0] += 1
    if not cond:
        FAILS.append(f"{name}: {detail}")


def close(a, b, name, rtol=1e-8, atol=1e-10):
    a = np.asarray(a, dtype=float)
    b = np.asarray(b, dtype=float)
    CHECKS[0] += 1
    if a.shape != b.shape:
        FAILS.append(f"{name}: shape {a.shape} vs {b.shape}")
        return
    if not np.allclose(a, b, rtol=rtol, atol=atol, equal_nan=True):
        with np.errstate(invalid='ignore', divide='ignore'):
            rel = np.nanmax(np.abs(a - b) / np.maximum(np.abs(b), 1e-300))
        FAILS.append(f"{name}: maxrel={rel:.4g}")


def angle_close(a, b, name, tol=1e-7):
    CHECKS[0] += 1
    d = (float(a) - float(b) + np.pi / 2) % np.pi - np.pi / 2
    if abs(d) > tol:
        FAILS.append(f"{name}: angle diff {d:.3g}")

    lab[((yy - 16) / 9.) ** 2 + ((xx - 22) / 6.) ** 2 < 1] = 1
    lab[8:11, 26:33] = 1
    lab[15:18, 20:23] = 0            # hole
    out['ellipse_bump_hole'] = lab

    # region touching the coordinate origin (bbox start == 0)
    lab = np.zeros((20, 24), dtype=np.int32)
    lab[0:7, 0:9] = 1
    lab[2:4, 9:13] = 1
    out['at_origin'] = lab

    # region touching the far corner
    lab = np.zeros((18, 22), dtype=np.int32)
    lab[11:18, 15:22] = 1
    out['at_far_corner'] = lab

    # single pixel + two-pixel line + multiple labels
    lab = np.zeros((15, 17), dtype=np.int32)
    lab[3, 5] = 1
    lab[7:9, 2] = 2
    lab[10:14, 8:15] = 3
    out['degenerate_multi'] = lab

    # random blob
    lab = np.zeros((26, 29), dtype=np.int32)
    blob = rng.random((26, 29)) < 0.55
    from scipy import ndimage as ndi
    blob = ndi.binary_closing(blob, np.ones((3, 3)))
    l, n = ndi.label(blob)
    sizes = ndi.sum(blob, l, range(1, n + 1))
    lab[l == (np.argmax(sizes) + 1)] = 1
    out['random_blob'] = lab

    # 3D ellipsoid, offset, with bump
    lab3 = np.zeros((13, 15, 17), dtype=np.int32)
    zz, yy, xx = np.mgrid[0:13, 0:15, 0:17]
    lab3[((zz - 6) / 4.) ** 2 + ((yy - 8) / 5.) ** 2 + ((xx - 9) / 6.) ** 2 < 1] = 1
    lab3[1:4, 2:5, 3:6] = 1
    out['ellipsoid3d'] = lab3

    # 3D bar at the origin
    lab3 = np.zeros((9, 11, 12), dtype=np.int32)
    lab3[0:4, 0:9, 0:3] = 1
    out['bar3d'] = lab3
    return out

# -------------------------------- 2. analytic scaling laws vs unit spacing
def unit_props(lab, inten, label):
    return [p for p in regionprops(lab, intensity_image=inten) if p.label == label][0]


for name, lab in MASKS.items():
    ndim = lab.ndim
    spacings = SPACINGS_2D[1:] if ndim == 2 else SPACINGS_3D[1:]
    rng = np.random.default_rng(11)
    inten = rng.random(lab.shape).astype(np.float64) * 5 + 1
    for spacing in spacings:
        s = np.asarray(spacing, float)
        for reg in regionprops(lab, intensity_image=inten, spacing=spacing):
            base = unit_props(lab, inten, reg.label)
            tag = f"[scale {name} label={reg.label} spacing={spacing}]"
            # coordinates and centroids scale componentwise
            close(reg.centroid, np.asarray(base.centroid) * s, f"{tag} centroid")
            close(reg.centroid_local, np.asarray(base.centroid_local) * s,
                  f"{tag} centroid_local")
            close(reg.centroid_weighted,
                  np.asarray(base.centroid_weighted) * s,
                  f"{tag} centroid_weighted")
            close(reg.centroid_weighted_local,
                  np.asarray(base.centroid_weighted_local) * s,
                  f"{tag} centroid_weighted_local")
            close(reg.coords, np.asarray(base.coords) * s, f"{tag} coords")
            # centroid decomposition: local + physical bbox origin
            start = np.asarray([sl.start for sl in reg.slice], float)
            close(reg.centroid, np.asarray(reg.centroid_local) + start * s,
                  f"{tag} centroid decomposition")
            close(reg.centroid_weighted,
                  np.asarray(reg.centroid_weighted_local) + start * s,
                  f"{tag} weighted centroid decomposition")
            # areas
            close(reg.area, base.area * np.prod(s), f"{tag} area")
            close(reg.area_bbox, base.area_bbox * np.prod(s), f"{tag} area_bbox")
            close(reg.area_convex, base.area_convex * np.prod(s),
                  f"{tag} area_convex")
            close(reg.area_filled, base.area_filled * np.prod(s),
                  f"{tag} area_filled")
            close(reg.pixel_area, np.prod(s), f"{tag} pixel_area")
            close(reg.extent, base.extent, f"{tag} extent invariance")
            close(reg.solidity, base.solidity, f"{tag} solidity invariance")
            check(reg.euler_number == base.euler_number,
                  f"{tag} euler invariance")
            # raw/central moments scale as prod(s_k ** p_k)
            for kind in ('moments', 'moments_central', 'moments_weighted',
                         'moments_weighted_central'):
                mm = reg[kind]
                bb = base[kind]
                factor = np.ones_like(bb, dtype=float)
                for powers in np.ndindex(bb.shape):
                    factor[powers] = np.prod(s ** np.asarray(powers))
                close(mm, bb * factor, f"{tag} {kind} scaling", rtol=1e-7)
            # normalized moments: dimensionless common-unit convention
            for kind in ('moments_normalized', 'moments_weighted_normalized'):
                mm = reg[kind]
                bb = base[kind]
                factor = np.ones_like(bb, dtype=float)
                for powers in np.ndindex(bb.shape):
                    factor[powers] = (np.prod(s ** np.asarray(powers))
                                      / min(s) ** sum(powers))
                close(mm, bb * factor, f"{tag} {kind} scaling", rtol=1e-7)
            # inertia tensor: quadratic in the intervals
            T = reg.inertia_tensor
            T0 = base.inertia_tensor
            if ndim == 2:
                factor = np.array([[s[1] ** 2, s[0] * s[1]],
                                   [s[0] * s[1], s[0] ** 2]])
                close(T, T0 * factor, f"{tag} inertia_tensor scaling")
            if len(set(s.tolist())) == 1:  # isotropic: lengths scale linearly
                k = s[0]
                close(reg.inertia_tensor, T0 * k ** 2,
                      f"{tag} isotropic inertia_tensor")
                close(reg.inertia_tensor_eigvals,
                      np.asarray(base.inertia_tensor_eigvals) * k ** 2,
                      f"{tag} isotropic eigvals")
                close(reg.axis_major_length, base.axis_major_length * k,
                      f"{tag} isotropic axis_major_length")
                close(reg.axis_minor_length, base.axis_minor_length * k,
                      f"{tag} isotropic axis_minor_length")
                close(reg.equivalent_diameter_area,
                      base.equivalent_diameter_area * k,
                      f"{tag} isotropic equivalent_diameter")
                close(reg.feret_diameter_max, base.feret_diameter_max * k,
                      f"{tag} isotropic feret")
                if ndim == 2:
                    close(reg.eccentricity, base.eccentricity,
                          f"{tag} isotropic eccentricity")
                    angle_close(reg.orientation, base.orientation,
                                f"{tag} isotropic orientation")
                    close(reg.perimeter, base.perimeter * k,
                          f"{tag} isotropic perimeter")
                    close(reg.perimeter_crofton, base.perimeter_crofton * k,
                          f"{tag} isotropic perimeter_crofton")
                    # dimensionless descriptors must be unchanged by a
                    # uniform change of measurement unit
                    close(reg.moments_normalized, base.moments_normalized,
                          f"{tag} isotropic moments_normalized invariance")
                    close(reg.moments_weighted_normalized,
                          base.moments_weighted_normalized,
                          f"{tag} isotropic weighted normalized invariance")

rng = np.random.default_rng(5)
for shape, spacings in [((13,), [(1.,), (0.3,), (7.5,)]),

                        ((7, 9, 8), SPACINGS_3D[1:]),
                        ((5, 6, 4, 7), [(1., 1., 1., 1.), (0.5, 2., 1.5, 0.25)])]:
    img = rng.random(shape)

    for spacing in spacings:
        s = np.asarray(spacing, float)
        tag = f"[func ndim={ndim} spacing={spacing}]"
        # raw moments against explicit summation
        grids = np.meshgrid(*[np.arange(n) * si for n, si in zip(shape, s)],
                            indexing='ij')
        Mraw = moments(img, order=3, spacing=spacing)
        for powers in np.ndindex(Mraw.shape):
            term = img.copy()
            for ax, pw in enumerate(powers):
                term = term * grids[ax] ** pw
            close(Mraw[powers], term.sum(), f"{tag} moments{powers}", rtol=1e-8)
        # centroid consistency
        c = centroid(img, spacing=spacing)
        expected_c = [(img * g).sum() / img.sum() for g in grids]
        close(c, expected_c, f"{tag} centroid")
        # implicit centering must use the physical centroid
        mu_auto = moments_central(img, order=3, spacing=spacing)
        mu_expl = moments_central(img, center=c, order=3, spacing=spacing)
        close(mu_auto, mu_expl, f"{tag} moments_central implicit center",
              rtol=1e-6, atol=1e-12)
        # explicit summation for central moments
        cg = np.meshgrid(*[np.arange(n) * si - ci
                           for n, si, ci in zip(shape, s, c)], indexing='ij')
        for powers in np.ndindex(mu_auto.shape):
            term = img.copy()
            for ax, pw in enumerate(powers):
                term = term * cg[ax] ** pw
            close(mu_auto[powers], term.sum(), f"{tag} mu{powers}",
                  rtol=1e-6, atol=1e-10)
        # normalized moments definition
        nu = moments_normalized(mu_auto, 3, spacing=spacing)
        mu0 = mu_auto.ravel()[0]
        u = min(s)
        for powers in np.ndindex(nu.shape):
            pw = sum(powers)
            if pw < 2:
                check(np.isnan(nu[powers]), f"{tag} nu{powers} nan")

                close(nu[powers],
                      (mu_auto[powers] / u ** pw) / mu0 ** (pw / ndim + 1),
                      f"{tag} nu{powers}", rtol=1e-8)

The `measure` snapshot supports a physical sampling grid via `spacing=`, so region coordinates are meant to be physical, `x_k = i_k · s_k` (paper §"Coordinate and moment definitions").
